record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Characterize QSOs arising from the graph construction
record.original_question: Let G be a finite graph with maximal connected components, let Phi be a finite allele set, let Omega be the set of configurations sigma: L -> Phi, and let mu be a strictly positive probability measure on Omega. For cells sigma_1 and sigma_2, define heredity coefficients by normalizing mu over the configurations whose restrictions to each connected component agree with either sigma_1 or sigma_2; these coefficients define a QSO V_mu on the simplex of probability measures on Omega. Which quadratic stochastic operators arise from this graph-configuration-measure construction, and how can the resulting class be characterized exactly?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(L,E)$ be a finite graph with vertex set $L$, and let $L=\bigsqcup_{i=1}^k L_i$ be its decomposition into maximal connected components. Let $\Phi$ be a finite set (the "allele set"), and let $\Omega=\Phi^L$ denote the set of all configurations $\sigma:L\to\Phi$. For each component $L_i$ and a configuration $\sigma\in\Omega$, write $\sigma|_{L_i}$ for the restriction of $\sigma$ to $L_i$. Fix a strictly positive probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ (so $\mu(\sigma)>0$ for every $\sigma\in\Omega$).

For any two configurations ("cells") $\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in\Omega$ and any $\sigma\in\Omega$, define the heredity coefficient
$$P(\sigma_1,\sigma_2;\sigma)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}\frac{\mu\bigl(\{\tau\in\Omega:\tau|_{L_i}=\sigma|_{L_i}\text{ and }\tau\text{ agrees with }\sigma_1\text{ or }\sigma_2\text{ on the remaining components in the appropriate sense}\}\bigr)}{\text{normalising factor}},$$
where the coefficients $P(\sigma_1,\sigma_2;\sigma)\ge 0$ are obtained by normalising $\mu$ over the configurations whose restriction to each connected component of $G$ coincides with the corresponding restriction of either $\sigma_1$ or $\sigma_2$, and satisfy $P(\sigma_1,\sigma_2;\sigma)=P(\sigma_2,\sigma_1;\sigma)$ and $\sum_{\sigma\in\Omega}P(\sigma_1,\sigma_2;\sigma)=1$.

Let $S(L,\Phi)$ denote the simplex of probability measures on $\Omega$. The associated quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V_\mu:S(L,\Phi)\to S(L,\Phi)$ is defined by
$$(V_\mu \ell)(\sigma)=\sum_{\sigma_1,\sigma_2\in\Omega}P(\sigma_1,\sigma_2;\sigma)\,\ell(\sigma_1)\,\ell(\sigma_2),\qquad \ell\in S(L,\Phi).$$

A QSO on $S(L,\Phi)$ in general is any map of this form with arbitrary nonnegative coefficients $P(\sigma_1,\sigma_2;\sigma)$ satisfying the symmetry and stochastic conditions above.

Problem: Characterise exactly the class of quadratic stochastic operators on $S(L,\Phi)$ that arise from the construction $\mu\mapsto V_\mu$ described above, as $G$, $\Phi$, and the strictly positive measure $\mu$ vary. That is, give necessary and sufficient conditions on a QSO $V$ for there to exist a finite graph $G$, finite allele set $\Phi$, and strictly positive measure $\mu$ on $\Phi^L$ such that $V=V_\mu$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the survey on quadratic stochastic operators (Ganikhodzhaev–Mukhamedov–Rozikov), and subsequent literature on QSOs corresponding to graphs (e.g., Lobachevskii J. Math. 2013) studies properties of such operators but does not provide a full characterization of which QSOs arise from this graph-configuration-measure construction. No source found that resolves this characterization problem.
